text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm putting together a small generator to consolidate all autoscale examples into a single canonical page. Will remove duplicated YAMLs across dedicated docs. PR later today. @devon @samir any objections?

devon: Love it. Can we keep separate sections for burst vs steady policies? Some customers only want burst examples.

samir: No objections. Please include tenant-label examples + eviction interaction — that's where readers get confused.

maria: Yes — planning sections: steady, burst, reserved-pool, tenant-labeling + eviction notes. Will also add a short terraform + SDK snippet. Ping me with code you want included.

jen: I can help with SDK snippets. Prefer Node + Python examples. Small example: createScalePolicy(...)

samir: Here’s a minimal YAML snippet for a burst policy to copy into the page:

```yaml
scalePolicy:
  name: burst-warmup
  type: reactive
  targets:
    cpu_utilization: 0.75
  burst:
    max_instances: 10
    cooldown: 60s
  labels:
    tenant: "analytics"
```

maria: Perfect, I'll adapt that. Could we also show eviction priority mapping? e.g. label `isolation=dedicated` gets higher priority than `isolation=shared`.

teo: Note: SLA wording needs to be explicit — "best-effort" vs "SLA-backed" for reserved pools. Docs team asked for a standard phrasing to avoid legal confusion.

maria: Agreed. I'll add a callout and link to the SLA wording draft: https://redwood-internal/handbook/dedicated-sla#draft

docs-bot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4321 — autoscale-generator + snippets. CI: docs-lint passing, linkcheck failing (1 broken link).

devon: Nice. Which link is failing? I'll fix it.

docs-bot: Broken link: /docs/dedicated/provisioning#old-terraform-sample -> 404

devon: I'll push a tiny redirect fix in the `docs` repo in a follow-up commit.

jen: For the SDK snippet, can we use this Node example? Will paste small code for inclusion:

```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.dedicated.createScalePolicy({
  poolId: "pool-123",
  name: "burst-warmup",
  policy: { type: "reactive", targets: { cpu: 0.75 }, burst: { max: 10 } }
});
```

maria: Thanks jen — I'll include both Node + Python alongside the YAML, and a short Terraform resource mapping. Any volunteers to sanity-check the TF snippet?

samir: I can check TF. Small nit: prefer `cooldown = \"60s\"` formatting in HCL example.

maria: Great. Tagging reviewers: @devon @samir @jen. I'll wait until the redirect fix lands before merging. ETA EOD.

devon: :thumbsup:
